LESSON: WRITING 12.5.1 THE WRITING PROCESS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.5: Writing 12.5.1 The writing process
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 12.5.1 The writing process, part of Strand 12 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can a good dialogue be written? 2. Why should one write a dialogue?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 12.5.1 The writing process together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner works in a team to brainstorm aspects of modern fashion.

• Critical thinking: It is developed as the learner solves simple problems when creating a dialogue on modern fashion.

Values:
Unity: It is promoted as the learner generates topics for dialogues in their groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Effective communication: It is developed as the learner expresses themselves through well written dialogues

Link to other Learning Areas:

Dialogue writing is relvant to the skills of scripting in Creative arts and sports.
